editorial:
Imagine taking a group of Girl Scouts into the woods for a fun trip, only to find out the local campfire stories are actually true. You follow a troop leader who thinks she has everything under control, but the vibe shifts quickly from a cute camping trip to a total nightmare. The movie does a great job of making you feel the creepiness of the forest. It sets up a sense of dread that makes you keep watching, wondering exactly what is hiding in the shadows of Bull Mountain.

What really works here is how the tension builds up before the scary parts hit. The acting feels natural, and the pacing keeps you on your toes without dragging. While it is a short film, it packs a punch. It is a perfect pick for a rainy Friday night when you want a quick scare.
endingExplained: The story ends when the leader realizes the legend of Bull Mountain is real and deadly. After trying to keep her scouts safe, she discovers that the monster is not just a story used to scare kids. In the final moments, the creature attacks, showing that no one is truly safe in these woods. The movie wraps up with a dark twist that leaves you feeling uneasy about the fate of the characters.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quick horror shorts and creepy urban legends.
